lines.en: An atmosphere that had grown frighteningly heavy. Whatever Hades was thinking, he said nothing for a long time. I struggled to hide my anxiety.
「Kim Dokja thought. This is the first hurdle.」
Hades finally spoke when the air around us had grown as heavy as it could.
[The 'real Gigantomachia'······. Do you understand the weight of those words?]
“I do.”
<Gigantomachia>, hosted by the great nebula <Olympus>.
A festival of the <Star Stream> in which five or six giants of lower Status imprisoned in <Tartarus> were released into the world, then hunted to savor an ancient victory······.
Hades spoke.
[The wars ended long ago. The gods won both <Titanomachia> and <Gigantomachia>.]
Hades was right.
The real wars had ended thousands of years ago.
[That is already 'settled history'. What meaning is there in bringing it back? Why do you wish to bring about <Gigantomachia>?]
“······That's what I'd like to ask. Why do the constellations of 'Olympus' keep staging a false <Gigantomachia>?”
“They summon giants to die in the scenario, kill them, and clumsily reenact that ancient battle. Why insist on calling that scenario <Gigantomachia>?”
Ruuuumble!
My knees shook involuntarily beneath Hades's furious 'Status'.
Standing some distance away, Persephone looked between Hades and me in alarm. Just as she was about to speak, I shook my head at her.
I couldn't accept help here.
We had to rely on our own strength and hold out without kneeling.
[The Giant Story 'Demon Realm's Spring' protects its Supreme Storytellers.]
It might not compare to Hades's 「Underworld」, but we had a story too.
A story we had built with our own strength.
With the strength of that story, I stood against Hades.
“It's because they're afraid, isn't it?”
The great nebulas were terrifying, powerful beings.
They were also the greatest cowards in the <Star Stream>.
“They must be afraid those 'giants' will rise up again. That's why they drag out the souls of those already dead and trample them, then trample them again, reliving their ugly triumph.”
There were many ways to make the 'real thing' disappear.
One was to create countless 'fakes'.
Worthless, commonplace fakes.
Through endless copies, a desperate battle had become a game.
A meaningless 'story', a laughingstock to everyone.
<Gigantomachia> had lost its authenticity long ago.
It had become a 'scenario' no constellation truly feared.
I looked up at Hades and asked,
“'Father of the Rich Night'. How much longer will you let <Olympus> use the giants of <Tartarus> as toys?”
A being counted among the three chief gods of <Olympus>, despite not belonging to it.
I recalled what 'Ways of Survival' had said about him.
「Hades had supplied countless giants for <Gigantomachia>, but had never once participated in the scenario himself.」
This ancient king of the Underworld must have watched the suffering of the giants in his prison for a very long time.
「That was why Hades knew the prisoners' sorrow and understood their pain. Like a prison guard reformed by his prisoners.」
“On my last visit, I saw you preparing a Giant Soldier (巨神兵) underground in Tartarus. Weren't you preparing for this very moment?”
[······You presume too much.]
Hades would have explained the existence of the 'Giant Soldier' to the twelve seats of Olympus like this: he was building it as a precaution, in case the giants ever started another war.
But I knew what Hades really thought.
“I know you hate the twelve seats.”
“They call you one of the three chief gods, but to them you're only a 'prison guard' who takes their problems off their hands.”
Perhaps the world's oldest prison guard was no different from a prisoner.
Hades looked down at me in silence.
[<Gigantomachia> is a dreadful war.]
“I know.”
[When the 'real Gigantomachia' begins, the 'giants' will not be the only toys of the scenario. Everyone there will become part of a 'Giant Story'.]
Hades continued, his eyes looking as though they had witnessed some distant destruction.
[The dokkaebis will run rampant, and the <Star Stream> will undergo an upheaval. The long-established power relations among the 'nebulas' will collapse.]
“I know that too.”
[What do you hope to gain by putting that terrible suffering on display for the world?]
I wasn't the one who answered.
[The Story 'King of a Kingless World' begins its story.]
[The Story 'One Who Opposes the Extraordinary' begins its story.]
[The Story 'Demon King of Salvation' begins its story.]
[The Giant Story 'Demon Realm's Spring' begins its story.]
All the Stories I had built until now were answering for me.
······Among them was one I had never seen before.
[The Story 'Life and Death Companions' begins its story.]
Every story ultimately flowed toward the ending it deserved.
[······Such a small human dreams an astonishing dream.]
“The smaller you are, the bigger you should dream.”
[You know of 'Stage Transformation,' I assume.]
I nodded. I already knew what Hades was going to say.

[The giants cannot win. The ancient heroes who were once the gods' 'incarnations' will appear again. The moment they clash with the giants, 'Stage Transformation' will begin, and history's tragedy will repeat itself.]
“We have heroes on our side too. Isn't a stage there to be smashed?”
Yoo Joonghyuk frowned when our eyes met.
Hades spoke again.
[One decisive problem remains.]
“You mean the principal actors who'll take the stage.”
I looked down at the palace floor. Below this ancient prison, the old protagonists of <Gigantomachia> would be waiting for me.
[Do you think they want 'Gigantomachia'?]
“It will begin as 'Gigantomachia', but it'll end differently.”
I answered with a quiet smile.
“And if they don't want it, I'll have to make them want it.”
After Kim Dokja disappeared, Han Sooyoung was kept busy calming the others.
“Fuck, do they think I'm their nanny?”
Lee Gilyoung and Shin Yoosung sat slumped on the ground. Between the children, Lee Hyunsung had curled up his enormous body and was muttering something.
Han Sooyoung sighed and snapped at them.
“Hey! Pull yourselves together. Yoo Joonghyuk went with him this time.”
Of course, it didn't work.
“Dokja-hyung······. Dokja-hyung, again······.”
“I knew we should've locked him up again back then······.”
While Lee Jihye and Lee Seolhwa soothed the children, Han Sooyoung racked her brains over their immediate problems.
With Kim Dokja and Yoo Joonghyuk dragged away, she would have to handle all the preparations for <Gigantomachia> over the remaining week.
“I really ought to start <Han Sooyoung Corporation>······.”
[A message has arrived through the 'Unidentifiable Wall.']
It was a message from Jang Hayoung.
—Hey. Han Sooyoung, how've you been?
It had been a while since she'd heard from Jang Hayoung, and the message made Han Sooyoung perk up.
Come to think of it, it was about time for the transcendents' group to return.
—Where are you guys now?
—We were just about to head back to Earth.
—Hurry up and get back here.
With no one else to vent to, Han Sooyoung began pouring out her pent-up frustration through the 'Unidentifiable Wall'. What had happened in the meantime, what had happened to the others······.
Han Sooyoung rarely talked about herself, but oddly enough, she tended to become talkative when speaking through this 'Wall.' It almost felt like counseling.
—······So, to sum it up, Kim Dokja came back, then disappeared again?
The window suddenly expanded, and the message window of the 'Wall' became a video screen.
The screen showed Jang Hayoung and the Breaking the Sky Sword Master, who was barking away.
—Hey! Why are you only telling me now? When did Kim Dokja get back?
—That's not what's important right now······.
The next moment, heavy static filled the screen and a different voice took over.
At first she wiped the screen, thinking an insect had landed on it. A closer look revealed that the insect was talking.
—Did you say that disciple of mine has returned?
A tiny man seated on the head of the enthusiastically barking Breaking the Sky Sword Master shouted in an imperious voice.
—Show me that brat at once. As the leader of the White Purity Sect, I shall severely punish him for failing to seek his master out first······!
The next moment, someone pulled the insect out of view. A small mountain appeared on the screen instead.
No, on closer inspection, it wasn't a mountain.
It was someone's nose.
—Where did you say that pale fellow went?
······This seemed to be the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint.
Han Sooyoung explained what had just happened as briefly as she could. After hearing her out, the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint thought for a moment, then answered.
—If he was taken from territory under <Olympus>'s jurisdiction······ he'd be locked up in <Tartarus>. There's no need to worry much, then.
Han Sooyoung was a little surprised by how calm her voice was.
But before she could respond, the enormous nose gazed off somewhere and murmured wistfully.
—······I wonder how they're doing.
Yoo Joonghyuk and I were promptly thrown onto the first floor of Tartarus.
With a playful expression, Persephone tapped my head and said,
[Demon King of Salvation, winning the giants over will not be easy.]
“······You seem to be enjoying this.”
[It has been a long time since anything this big happened in <Olympus>. I could help you behind my husband's back, but where would the fun be in that?]
“No, we'd be grateful if you hel—”
[May the story bless you, Demon King of Salvation.]
I'd expected her not to help.
The <Underworld> must not officially enter the war in this 'scenario'.
If the <Underworld> declared its participation in <Gigantomachia>, the war's scale and probability limit would expand beyond control.
So this war had to remain a 'rebellion' conducted with the <Underworld>'s tacit approval.

We crossed the first floor of <Tartarus>. Prisoners were still hard at work building Giant Soldiers throughout the floor. A few glanced at us, but none showed much interest. They probably took us for new prisoners.
“Do you think you can persuade the giants?”
“I don't know either. We're on our way to find out.”

The underground prison of <Tartarus> held beings beyond imagination. Not only giants, but constellations and transcendents who had opposed <Olympus> and committed all manner of atrocities. Some were monsters that Yoo Joonghyuk and I could never defeat with our current strength.
“It will be difficult. Especially within a week.”
“We'll manage somehow. ······Don't you have someone to meet here too?”
Yoo Joonghyuk glared at me as if asking how I knew.
If I remembered correctly, the being who had taught Yoo Joonghyuk 'Giant Body Transformation' in a previous round was here.
“I have someone to meet too. Someone I need to recruit as a companion.”
“A companion?”
“Someone I'd never have taken as a companion before. But life has changed my mind.”
We stopped at the same time. We had no choice.
Something enormous was blocking our path.
“······Don't tell me you mean that dog.”
An enormous guard dog blocked the door to the second underground floor. Cerberus, the three-headed monster dog.
I quietly looked up at the dog. More precisely, at the enormous Giant Soldier busily stroking its heads. One of Cerberus's heads was enthusiastically chewing on the Giant Soldier's forearm.
[Hahaha! Yellowy! Bite!]
[That hardly even hurts!]
Armor of dull, dark metal.
A Story weapon Hades himself had used in the original rounds.
“Hey.”
When I waved, the Giant Soldier turned toward us. It shuddered in apparent surprise, then answered in a voice filled with delight.
[······Subway grasshopper guy? Hahaha! You finally croaked, huh? Didn't you?]
I smiled wryly.
To win <Gigantomachia>, we absolutely needed that plastic-model otaku's help.
“I came to get you, Kim Namwoon.”
[······Get me? Why?]
“I need you.”
Kim Namwoon looked down at me as though I'd said something utterly absurd.
Now that I'd said it, I felt strange too.
Well, I'd never imagined saying it myself.
I recalled Kim Namwoon of the 1863rd round. The white-haired man who liked Lee Jihye and muddled along with the others. Immature, inconsiderate, and deeply wrapped up in himself.
「Kim Namwoon is evil. That fact has not changed.」
I had seen another possibility for Kim Namwoon there, but that hadn't completely overturned my prejudice against him.
It was my conversation with Han Sooyoung in the 1863rd round that had made me decide to use him.
—You'll never reach Scenario 95 with that softhearted attitude.
Han Sooyoung, Yoo Joonghyuk, and I were different.
But if there was one thing we all agreed on, it was that every story had moments when you had to pursue efficiency.
[The constellation 'Secretive Plotter' takes an interest in your choice.]
[The constellation 'Abyssal Black Flame Dragon' takes an interest in the incarnation 'Kim Namwoon.']
There was no message from Uriel, so she was probably busy teaching Jung Heewon.
Jung Heewon would blow her top again if she knew I'd come here. Good thing I'd left her in Eden.
Kim Namwoon spoke.
[No. Why should I help you?]
I'd known he would say that.
“Suit yourself. Let's go, Yoo Joonghyuk.”
I approached Cerberus with Yoo Joonghyuk.
[What? Where are you going?]
“Downstairs.”
[Hahaha, you're joking, right? My Yellowy's glaring right at you······!]
As if to prove his point, the half-dozing Cerberus bared its teeth at us. Almost simultaneously, Yoo Joonghyuk activated [Breaking the Sky Swordsmanship].
Kwoooom!
Before, even fighting the Cerberus on the first underground floor would have been difficult. Now, things were different.
“······You could've gone a little easier.”
“We have no time to waste here.”
Cerberus, felled by a single blow, lay with its tongue hanging out. Prisoners startled by the explosion began shouting, and alarms blared everywhere.
Normally, the judges would have come running by now, but with Hades's tacit agreement, we should be safe for a while.
We passed the fallen Cerberus and went down to the second floor.
[You crazy······ crazy bastards!]
Kim Namwoon's flustered voice rang out.
Yoo Joonghyuk glanced at me and asked,
—······Are we leaving him? That Giant Soldier is useful.
—Just watch.
We immediately began descending the spiral staircase to the second underground floor.
The abyss opening beneath the staircase had no visible bottom.
Legend said Tartarus was so unfathomably deep that an anvil dropped into it would fall for nine days.
[Wait, take me with you!]
Kim Namwoon hurried after us. The Giant Soldier had shrunk to a little over two meters. Pluto could adjust its size for its user's convenience.
I asked teasingly,
“Why follow us? I thought you said no.”
[Well······ I was a little bored.]
His mouth kept curling into a grin; he seemed unable to hide his feelings.
[So what are we doing? How far down are we going? Huh?]
“To meet the giants.”
[What?]
After a moment of blank surprise, Kim Namwoon shouted.
[Ha······ hahahaha! Wow, subway grasshopper guy! I knew it back then, but you really are crazy. Do you know what the giants are?]
Of course I did.
[If someone like you meets those ■■, they'll put a hole in your ■■ and you'll be ■■ right away······.]
[Prisoner filtering has activated!]
[This content has been filtered to promote proper language use in Tartarus.]
[Prisoner 'Kim Namwoon' receives 1 penalty point.]
[Oh, fu■!]
[Prisoner 'Kim Namwoon' receives 2 penalty points.]
Even without Kim Namwoon's profanity, I knew very well what giants were.
Giants (巨神).
The race that had ruled the Age of Gold (金) in the early days of <Olympus>.
Roooooar—!

A dizzying roar rang out as though on cue, stopping me in my tracks. Far below, the giants had already sensed our presence and were reacting. Even a fraction of the 'Status' in that roar sent chills down my spine.
[You're crazy. Crazy······.]
Ignoring Kim Namwoon, I called Biyoo. She wriggled and popped out from inside my clothes.
[Baat?]
“You're managing access to the channel, right?”
[Baat!]
“Everything broadcast from the <Underworld> is off the record. Only admit constellations who've sworn not to disclose any information.”

Biyoo nodded with a baaat and began working the channel controls. A few constellations complained, but this was the right approach for now. The less the outside world learned about what happened next, the better.
Before long, several constellations sent messages.
[The constellation 'Prisoner of the Golden Headband' grumbles and agrees to the oath.]
[The constellation 'Abyssal Black Flame Dragon' smacks his lips in apparent displeasure and agrees to the oath.]
[The constellation 'Secretive Plotter' reports having already sworn an oath.]
Watching the messages pour in, Kim Namwoon exclaimed in wonder.
[Whoa, so this is what a channel's like······.]
Well, Kim Namwoon had died before 'Sponsor Selection' even began. The constellations' indirect messages would be a novelty to him.
Kim Namwoon chattered noisily throughout our descent.
[But I'm surprised Mister Underworld King let you come down here. That guy's a real stickler.]
“······You're noisy. Open your mouth once more and I'll cut you down.”
[······What, think you can fight? Wanna go a round?]
Conflicting emotions showed in Yoo Joonghyuk's eyes as he glared at Kim Namwoon.
Yoo Joonghyuk already knew him.
Of course he did. Kim Namwoon had been his companion in the previous round.
“Yoo Joonghyuk. We don't have time to waste our strength here. You know that, right?”
Kim Namwoon smacked his lips as Yoo Joonghyuk sheathed his sword.
Panting excitedly, he looked just like a child.
A child left alone after being neglected for a long time.
When I'd asked why she had used 'Kim Namwoon', Han Sooyoung of the 1863rd round had answered like this.
—No character is born a 'bad person.' The author just wrote them that way. Gave them a narrative that left them no choice but to become bad. I didn't like that.
I agreed with Han Sooyoung to some extent.
But the Kim Namwoon of this world had fastened that 'first button' in entirely the wrong buttonhole.
He had incited people on the subway and plotted the worst kind of crime.
[My heart's pounding. Haven't felt like this since Mom and Dad abandoned me at the same time.]
“······What kind of feeling is that?”
[Like a new adventure's waiting for me.]
Kim Namwoon had certainly been created.
Should I blame the author of 'Ways of Survival'?
Or should I blame myself for not doing enough to stop Kim Namwoon back then?
When I checked my smartphone, a new message was waiting.
[The 'fourth revision' is currently being updated.]
······I'd figured it would be updated soon. So much had happened that its silence had seemed strange.
As we descended, I opened the 'Ways of Survival' file and read the parts I needed.
Reading 'Ways of Survival' was always best when I felt anxious.
「Kim Dokja thought. The third round I'm living in no longer resembles any round of the original.」
I could probably find similarities if I really looked.
There had been many visits to the <Underworld> in the original 'Ways of Survival'.
The 47th, 211th, 397th rounds······. Countless ones, really.
But in none of them had he come to the <Underworld> at 'this particular point'.
「I need to gather every piece of information I can use.」
「Unless I persuade the giants, we can't win <Gigantomachia>.」
Traces of <Olympus> were scattered throughout the pages of 'Ways of Survival'.
Splitting the sea with a single gesture.
Trampling transcendents and constellations.
The monstrous twelve seats of Olympus, who ruthlessly shattered even planets.
Once I left this place, I would have to face them head-on.
Countless pieces of information flashed through my mind, sorting themselves into what I could and couldn't use.
“Kim Dokja.”
Yoo Joonghyuk studied me for a moment, then spoke quietly.
“Nothing.”
What was with him? That came out of nowhere.
I immediately activated [Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint], and Yoo Joonghyuk's thoughts came through clearly.
「He doesn't look confident.」
I felt self-conscious, as though he'd hit the mark. Maybe my emotions showed on my face more than I thought.
I deliberately raised my voice.
“There are two things we need from the <Underworld>. One's 'Giant's Armor (巨神鉀)', and the other's the 'Giant's Oath'.”
“······Neither will be easy.”
“Probably not.”
“But the harder it is, the better the reward.”
I chuckled at Yoo Joonghyuk's words.
Grrrrrr······!
Before long, the entrance to the Underworld's second floor appeared.
As expected, another Cerberus guarded the door. This one was larger than the one on the first floor.
Just as Yoo Joonghyuk drew his sword, Kim Namwoon shouted.
[Wait! Don't hit Yellowy!]
“······Move. We don't have time.”
Stroking Cerberus, Kim Namwoon turned to us and said,
[I know where the judges' orbital elevator is.]
An orbital elevator. 'Tartarus' certainly had such a device.
A hidden means of transport used only by the judges.
But not even 'Ways of Survival' described its exact location.
Somewhat doubtful, I asked,
“How do you know about it?”
[I've sneaked down in it myself.]
“How far?”
[The 77th floor.]
I was startled.
Floor 77 was the gateway straight to the lowest level.
[Follow me. This way.]
Yoo Joonghyuk and I exchanged looks as Kim Namwoon strode confidently ahead.
So this guy could actually be useful sometimes.
······Should I have spared him after all?
No, it seemed he was useful this time because he was dead. So had killing him been the right choice after all?

The orbital elevator was incredibly fast. The second underground floor, the third, the fourth······. It plunged downward, showing us the horrors of <Tartarus> along the way. Prisoners attacking one another, and demons amid terrible sulfurous flames, shouted at us.
“New blood!”
“Hey! What are you staring at? Eyes down!”

There were transcendents among the cackling prisoners. Like me, they had broken the law in territory under <Olympus>'s jurisdiction, or been captured for defying the twelve seats. Some of them would end up as steaks on the Gourmet Association's tables.
With a screech, the elevator stopped, and we got off on the 77th floor.
There were no prisoners on floor 77. A space like a vast cavern (空洞), so wide one couldn't even begin to measure it. A huge door stood at its center.
[No Yellowys from the 78th floor down. They'd be useless anyway.]
A mere Cerberus couldn't stop a giant.
A great monster like Campe might be another matter.
Kim Namwoon's bravado faded as he spoke hesitantly.
[······I've never been past there either. I stuck my hand in a little once, and this happened.]
I looked at the scar on the Giant Soldier's shoulder. It had nearly healed now, but it appeared to have taken a blow powerful enough to tear its arm off.

Although still incomplete, Giant Soldier Pluto was a fearsome weapon that could produce power comparable to that of a Narrative-grade constellation, even without a pilot. Beings capable of damaging such a weapon that badly were on the other side.
I approached the door. It stood well over thirty meters high, with a design resembling a human face.
Yoo Joonghyuk spoke.
“We need an offering to enter.”
Kim Namwoon flinched at his words.
[What? How do you know that?]
We ignored Kim Namwoon and continued.
“I know. I brought one.”
“Offer something too powerful and you'll summon the 'ancient giants'.”
“You'll have to meet them someday anyway.”
“······Not now. If we meet them now, we'll die.”
Even the arrogant Yoo Joonghyuk looked tense.
There were different kinds of giants in <Tartarus>.
One kind was the Titans, the 'ancient giants' who had once ruled <Olympus> and started <Titanomachia>. The other was the Gigantes, the giants who had started <Gigantomachia>.
If I had to compare their ranks, I'd say the gap was about the same as that between Myth-grade and Narrative-grade constellations.
The ones I needed to summon were the 'Gigantes'.
“Don't worry. Unless we offer a high-tier Star Relic, there's no way a Titan-class giant will······.”
That was when the ground began to quake.
[The structure of <Tartarus> is becoming unstable!]
Craaaack!
The moment I realized something was wrong, the door burst open and an enormous hand snatched Yoo Joonghyuk.
“Yoo Joonghyuk!”
Just as I reached for him, two more hands shot out through the door.
I hastily used [Electrification] to dodge them, but Kim Namwoon couldn't.
[Aaaaaah! Help!]
The next moment, more than ten hands descended on me at once. I tumbled helplessly within the enclosure they formed. When I regained my senses, I was hanging upside down in the air.
As my view swung back and forth, I saw the enormous arm holding me.
[The exclusive skill 'Fourth Wall' activates strongly!]
Amid the crackling sparks, a 'Status' so immense that I could barely breathe filled the surroundings.
A being that could burst me apart at any moment, if it so wished.
Something like a huge, blunt finger kept flicking my backside.
[A cute little gnat has come.]
An enormous eye resembling that of the 'Breaking the Sky Sword Saint' peered at me.
[Little child, who are you?]
Three of the many arms extending from the giant held me, Yoo Joonghyuk, and Kim Namwoon respectively.
Dangling in midair, I stared at the giant in disbelief.
······The door had opened that easily?
I couldn't understand it.

The door sealing the giants below the 77th underground floor was designed so it couldn't be opened from inside. That had held true in both the 47th and 211th rounds. That was why I'd prepared an offering in advance······.
[Hmm······. Probability is troublesome. It has been getting worse lately.]
With a crackle, probability sparks spread over the giant's entire body.

The giant pulled off one of its own fingers and threw it out through the door. As if waiting for that, the sparks rushed at the finger and melted it away. Then they slowly subsided······. It was unbelievable.
A single finger had covered the probability cost of the offering?
That had never been possible in any of Yoo Joonghyuk's rounds.
Whooooo······.
A faint aura rising from the giant's entire body. Although its Status was concealed, an immense, unfathomable 'Status' slumbered within.
One of the oldest things in the world.
A 'myth' accumulated through the ages.
Merely trying to gauge the years lingering on its surface made my heart tremble.
This was a Titan.
Unquestionably, an ancient giant.
The myths stirring across its bulk were badly worn with age, but still alive. Yet it looked very different from the original I knew.
「The ancient giants Yoo Joonghyuk met had always been in decline, on the verge of death.」
It was strange.
All giants lived by relying on the 'Giant Stories' of <Titanomachia> and <Gigantomachia>. As those myths lost influence, or their transmission grew more distorted, the giants' strength weakened too.
Because of <Olympus>'s habitual <Gigantomachia> events, their Giant Stories should have been considerably weakened by now.
[Child, do you not intend to answer? My patience is as deep as the sea, so I am quite good at waiting. Having waited so long already, I see no reason I cannot wait longer.]
But the voice of the giant before me held an unbelievable vitality.
A possibility suddenly occurred to me.
「Could I have come to the <Underworld> too early?」
This <Gigantomachia> hadn't happened yet. If that meant the giants' decline had yet to pass a critical point, it was entirely possible.
The giant continued.
[But······ I do not know if my friends will be as patient. It has been a very long time since children as delicious-looking as you came in.]
Kim Namwoon's jaw was trembling. Answering was beyond him.
The giant stroked his cheek as though it found him adorable.

[A child burdened with deep sins. Children like that are all the tastier to tear into. To become the body of a Giant Soldier of your own accord······. Are you perhaps the child who was torn into last time?]
Prisoners who fell into the depths while trying to escape <Tartarus> usually became food for the giants.
Kim Namwoon was shaking so badly that, had he been human, he would probably already have been foaming at the mouth.
The giant turned its gaze back to me.
[I smell many things on you. Constellations, angels, demons, humans······ and even Outer Gods. What sort of Story are you?]
I didn't answer.
Sometimes there were answers more definite than words.
Even before an 'ancient giant', I couldn't be cowed from the start.
[Releasing the Demon King's 'Status'!]
Ruuuumble!
Once I escaped the giant's grip, I could see it more clearly.
Its size surpassed anything I'd imagined.
It looked over a hundred meters tall······. A fight wouldn't even be a contest.
[I'll eat that child.]
[Let us tear him in half.]
Voices creeping out from all around.
I spoke coldly in warning.
“We're not food.”
“We have come to negotiate.”
Yoo Joonghyuk added his voice.
He too had escaped the giant's grasp, radiating the Status of a transcendent.
But the giant answered indifferently.
[That is not for you to decide.]
I'd expected this response.
That arrogance was what had ultimately brought the giants to ruin.
Without further delay, I used my True Voice.
[It is an honor to meet you, great 'Hundred-Handed (百手) Princes', the 'three Hecatoncheires brothers'.]
At my words, three hundred eyes opened at once in the darkness. Those eyes belonged to only 'three giants'.
The three giants spoke together.
[How interesting. You came here knowing who we are?]
Hundred-handed giants (百手巨神), each with fifty heads and a hundred arms.
I knew the names of these Titan giants.
